meta.title: Fermi TAM is customers times yearly price
meta.summary: SAMPLE 200k dentists × $600/year → $120M TAM; 1,000 customers is $600k ARR. Watch a 10× error in one factor.

success.message:
Session complete. Stack customers × yearly price, then take a believable slice. Watch 10× zeros.

SAMPLE: 200k×$600=$120M TAM; 1,000 customers=$600k ARR.

start.message:
SAMPLE: 200k dentists, $50/mo tool. Yearly TAM stack?

First?

choices.label: Use US population 330M as the customer count

wrong_start_monthly_tam.message:
That is a monthly ceiling. TAM talk is usually yearly: ×12 first.

Return to yearly.

wrong_start_pop.message:
Fermi TAM uses the reachable buyer, not census.

Return to yearly.

wrong_tam_12m.message:
200k×600: 2×6=12, then five zeros from 200,000 and two from 600 wait — 200,000×600=120,000,000.

Revisit the zeros.

wrong_tam_1_2b.message:
That would be 2M dentists or $6,000/year.

Revisit the zeros.

slice.message: You might get 1,000 of those dentists. ARR?

choices.label: Quote $120M as if it were your ARR

wrong_slice_tam_as_arr.message:
TAM is the pond. Your slice is customers × price.

Try the slice again.

wrong_slice_50k.message:
$50 is monthly. Yearly is $600 × 1,000 = $600k.

Try the slice again.
